summary.name: Lunar
summary.one_liner: Lunar is a macOS app that controls external monitor brightness, contrast, volume and input over DDC, with ambient-light, schedule and location-based adaptive modes.
use_cases: Adjust external monitor brightness from keyboard brightness keys
Sync external monitors with MacBook adaptive brightness
Turn off MacBook display when an external monitor is connected
Schedule monitor brightness by time, sunrise or sunset
Control monitor volume and input switching on a Mac
summary.what_it_does: Lunar sends DDC commands directly to external monitors to set hardware brightness and contrast, adjust volume, switch inputs and power off displays, rather than overlaying a black screen. Brightness and volume keys can control all displays or the one under the cursor. Pro features add Sync Mode (mirroring the MacBook's ambient-light adjustments to external monitors), Sensor Mode (using an external wireless ambient light sensor), Clock Mode and Location Mode (schedule- or sun-based adaptation), BlackOut (turning off selected displays via hotkey), and FaceLight (maximum brightness with a warm-white overlay for video calls). It also supports macOS Shortcuts and a command-line interface, and includes DisplayLink and Raspberry Pi workarounds for monitors that do not accept DDC.
notable: Uses DDC to change real monitor hardware brightness instead of a software black overlay
Sensor Mode uses a wireless external ambient light sensor for Macs without a built-in one
Sub-zero dimming goes below the monitor's 0% brightness
Command-line interface (lunar get/set/ddc/lux) and macOS Shortcuts integration
caveats: Many key features (Sync, Sensor, Clock, Location, BlackOut, FaceLight, XDR Brightness, Auto BlackOut) require Lunar Pro, listed at $23
Free version limits Manual Mode to 100 adjustments per day and Shortcuts to 100 action calls per day
DisplayLink setups need a Raspberry Pi and extra hardware for DDC control; DisplayLink software blocks DDC and gamma pass-through
Sensor Mode's built-in light sensor support is Apple Silicon only (for Location/Sensor features as stated)
